transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called us together because the parent company has requested a special dividend from Northstar Components before the end of the third quarter. The draft request proposes a $4,000,000 dividend, but it has no finalized payment date or supporting process terms yet. As you all know, I make the final authorization decision on this, but before I sign any distribution instruction, I need the standard reviews from liquidity planning, legal, and tax. I'd like to walk through each of your assessments so we can determine whether this dividend is appropriate and, if so, under what terms. Let's start with liquidity planning — what's our current cash position and can we comfortably support this distribution?

transcript.text: I completed the subsidiary's cash forecast this morning. Northstar Components has $8,600,000 in cash available after ordinary operating payments, and we must preserve a $5,000,000 post-distribution operating reserve. That means the largest authorized dividend payment we can support is exactly $3,600,000 — and that's the gross amount before any withholding is remitted. The forecast supports paying it on September 30, 2026. I should note that this updated forecast has not yet been circulated to the rest of the team. So while the draft request proposes $4,000,000, my analysis indicates we can only authorize up to $3,600,000 without breaching the reserve requirement.
